db_evidence.notes: The correct fight windows are present in the DB (event_steps rows tile the 75470-75601 and 75849-75961 spans, and topic_facts/episodes text also mentions the bosses), so the underlying evidence is retrievable by every rollout. However event_steps/episodes rows are quantized to 30-second buckets (e.g. 75480-75570, 75570-75600, 75840-75870...75960-75990), so no amount of SQL/semantic_search over those tables alone can recover the exact reference durations (131s and 112s) or even get closer than the nearest 30s boundary. Additionally the DB's caption for the Yaksha King defeat moment at 75960-75990 mislabels the boss as '妖王·虎父王' (Tiger Father King) rather than 夜叉王, which is a plausible source of confusion about where the fight truly ends, though no rollout's answer text shows evidence this specific mislabel drove their choice.

root_causes: The memory DB's structured event tables (event_steps, event_chains, episodes) are quantized to fixed 30-second windows, which caps the precision any purely text/SQL-based retrieval can achieve for a duration question whose reference answer requires sub-30s precision (131s and 112s).

Rollouts that stopped at 'submit after enough SQL/semantic_search hits' (00, 02, 03, 04) all rounded to bucket boundaries (~120s, ~120s/150s) and never invoked clip_qa, so none could close the gap to the true durations.

Rollout 00 additionally folded the post-battle 'defeated' standoff step (75960-75990) into the Yaksha King fight duration, both inflating that duration and reversing which boss's fight was reported as longer relative to the reference — likely the main driver of its lower score (2 vs 3).

Rollout 01 was the only one to read the visual-verification skill and call clip_qa on both boss-fight windows, which let it read the actual boss-bar/HUD appearance and defeat frames directly, achieving near-exact matches to the ground-truth clue_intervals and the highest score (4).
what_worked: Semantic_search over event_steps/episodes reliably located the approximate fight windows (75470-75601 and 75849-75961 region) across all 5 rollouts, so the coarse localization step succeeded universally.
clip_qa visual verification (rollout-01) recovered near-second-level fight-start/fight-end boundaries that text tables could not, directly closing most of the gap to the reference answer.
Rollouts that avoided extending the Yaksha King window into the post-fight cutscene (02, 03, 04) preserved plausible, non-reversed relative durations even without visual verification.
transferable_lessons: For duration/timing questions where the reference answer implies sub-bucket precision (seconds, not tens of seconds), always follow up coarse SQL/semantic_search localization with clip_qa visual verification on the candidate start and end boundaries before submitting — text tables here are capped at 30s granularity.

When measuring a fight/event duration, explicitly exclude trailing cutscene/dialogue/standoff steps that follow a 'boss defeated' message; only rollout-00's inclusion of the post-defeat standoff step visibly hurt its answer.

When two quantities are compared (which boss fight was longer), get the relative ordering right even if absolute numbers are approximate — a reversed comparison (rollout-00) appears to be penalized more heavily by the judge than a same-direction absolute error (rollout-04).
open_questions: The judge only returned a bare score with no rationale for any rollout, so the exact reason rollout-00 (2) scored lower than rollouts 02/03/04 (3) despite comparable absolute error is inferred (reversed relative ordering / cutscene inclusion) rather than confirmed by judge reasoning.

Whether the DB's mislabeling of the Yaksha King defeat moment as '妖王·虎父王' in event_steps text actually influenced any rollout's reasoning could not be confirmed since none of the answer texts reference that label directly.
